subject: Information Theory
title: Jensen-Shannon Divergence
description: A quick win: understand Jensen-Shannon Divergence.

hook.text: KL divergence isn't symmetric and can be infinite. Scientists needed a friendlier version. They built one.

buildup.text: Jensen-Shannon divergence averages two KL divergences: JSD(P||Q) = ½ D(P||M) + ½ D(Q||M), where M is the midpoint.

discovery.text: JSD is always finite, always symmetric, and its square root is a true mathematical distance metric.

twist.text: GANs (generative adversarial networks) originally used JSD to judge how realistic generated images looked.

climax.text: When comparing two distributions safely and symmetrically, JSD is the standard tool.

punchline.text: A kinder, symmetric version of KL divergence.

quiz.question: What advantage does Jensen-Shannon divergence have over KL divergence?
